lesson_core_move: Interpret causal convolution by connecting one-sided support and overlap bounds to the LTI output rule that only past input values weighted by the impulse response contribute at time t.

outline_section.learning_goal: Explain causal convolution as an LTI output rule where a one-sided impulse response makes only present and past input values contribute to y(t).

image_policy.image_description_seed: A single tau-axis schematic for fixed output time t showing the shaded past-input region tau <= t, x(tau) over the tau axis, and h(t - tau) as a one-sided weighting function that is zero for tau > t.

image_policy.image_generation_notes: Use one clean conceptual schematic with no decorative elements and no numerical signal values; the visual should reduce load by making the causal cutoff at tau = t visible.

tutorial_outline.direct_instruction_goal: State that if h is causal, then h(t - tau) is nonzero only when tau <= t, so convolution output y(t) uses only input values at the present or before the output time.
tutorial_outline.base_case: Use a generic input x(tau) and a causal impulse response h(t) = e^{-at}u(t) with t fixed.
paragraph_plan: Recall the convolution output formula and emphasize that t is fixed while tau is the integration variable.
Define causality for the impulse response as h(s) = 0 when s < 0, then apply it to the shifted argument s = t - tau.
Convert t - tau >= 0 into tau <= t and identify this as the causal support constraint on the shifted impulse response.
Explain that x(tau) values with tau > t are future input values, so they cannot affect the current output of a causal LTI system.
Connect the support constraint to the familiar overlap idea: y(t) accumulates only where x(tau) and h(t - tau) are both nonzero.
Name the interpretation that will drive the examples: causal convolution is accumulated weighted past input.
display_math_plan: Show h(s) = 0 for s < 0, so h(t - \tau) = 0 when t - \tau < 0.
Show the causal form y(t) = \int_{-\infty}^{t} x(\tau)h(t - \tau)\,d\tau before adding any extra support restrictions from x.

outline_section.handoff_notes: Keep the tutorial compact and direct. The section should establish the causal support rule, not compute a convolution integral.
